goal: Let independent review lenses reuse source-verified upstream suite evidence
asset: Red-team review scope and execution evidence
scope: Compact upstream execution pointers in reviewer and refuter context
Typed reused and own-run suite citations
Named reasons for independent suite reruns
outOfScope: Treating suite passes as adversarial review coverage
Claiming a known interpreter for opaque shell wrappers

record.question: How should review lenses use suites that upstream gates already ran?

options.strongest_objection: Every citation must bind an actual green row to the reviewed head and launch
Duplicate suites and setup compete for host capacity and consume most review wall time

record.rationale: Send compact candidate pointers, fetch exact source rows with the pinned witness and verify typed citations against the log; reviewers spend their budget on attacks and rerun only for named claims.
evidence: Issue #182 measured 138 of342 review wall minutes spent duplicating upstream gate work

costs.cost: Read source rows and verify citations, without suite execution
evidence: Attest rows already bind SHA, nonce, log and runtime identity

costs.cost: Measured41% redundant review wall time and shared-host contention

requirements.statement: Every typed suite claim names a verified upstream or own execution; reused rows can support many lenses at one head/nonce, mismatched red/stale/missing rows refuse clean recording, and own reruns name their claim
requirements.counterexample: A reviewer claims suite coverage with no execution or silently reruns a covered suite with no named claim

checks.scope: Emitted reviewer context, source attest rows, shared reuse and negative claim checks
assumptions: Worker attack quality remains semantic review; suite passes do not establish adversarial coverage

challenges.claim: Does reusing one suite row make two verification gates independent?
challenges.resolution: No. This reuse applies only to review evidence; independent prove nodes retain the one-execution-per-node rule.
